Source 95f421513ee961a1 §1, (1), and the vertical-plane paragraphs are the exact source. The note frames K as a convex body and builds its example by a convex hull.

For 1<h<2 the exact gap a−h=(2−h)(h+1)/(3(h−1)) is positive and direct integration gives zero x moment. Projection of the graph section onto the base is exactly D since x≤1<h, and the graph Jacobian is constant.

Both oblique orientations capture length 1−x/h on D and length two outside it. The inward raw normals are (−1/h,0,±1); dividing graph area by their norms gives |D|. Multiplying by their raw centroid margins and dividing by 2|B| gives the displayed s; complementing reverses that scalar.

A centered chord of convex B gives a section rectangle of area 4||q|| and centroid zero. The coarea vector after normalization by 2|B| is (2Rq/|B|,0), with the sign of the orientation encoded in R. Exact rational checks at h=3/2 give |D|=125/12, |B|=65/6, p=27/52 and s=125/6084.

The rational convex B contains the origin in its interior because D does. Since B is convex, its intersection with the line of two opposite boundary points q and −q is exactly their segment: any extension beyond either point would put that point in the interior of B by convexity and the interior origin. Transverse rational edge intersections supply rational endpoints.

The former nonconvex reading allowed a rational inward notch left of x=−h, giving a product outside the convex-body construction. The revised hypothesis excludes it. The original area and cap computations remain valid on the intended convex scope.
